description: The Volksbank-Bever-Lauf takes place on 27 June 2026 at the Beverstadion in Ostbevern. The event offers various races, including a half-marathon relay and individual races for runners born in 2012 or earlier. The course is measured by the DLV and is part of the Volksbank-Cup running series. Drinks and refreshments are available at the finish area, and changing and shower facilities are located directly at the Beverstadion.
course_highlights: Course measured by the DLV
Relay exchange zone at the Beverstadion
Start and finish at the Beverstadion in Ostbevern
additional: Late entries are possible on the day of the event from 2 p.m. until 30 minutes before the respective race, for an additional fee of €2. All athletes can enjoy running tea, mineral water, non-alcoholic beer and Fassbrause in the finish area. Changing and shower facilities are located directly at the Beverstadion. The relay exchange zone is at the Beverstadion. The event offers a pleasant running atmosphere, with refreshments, changing rooms and showers. Registration and results are available on the official website.

name: EWE Nordseelauf - Etappe 7
price_range: 37,00 € für Funktionsshirt (Preise variieren je nach Produkt und Zeitraum), sonst keine expliziten Teilnahmegebühren genannt
description: The EWE North Sea Run is a traditional stage race across seven different East Frisian Islands on the Lower Saxony North Sea coast. Over eight days, participants run, walk or Nordic walk approximately 10 kilometres per stage, enjoying the unique natural surroundings, maritime atmosphere and healthy offshore climate. The event attracts running enthusiasts from across Germany and abroad, offering a fair competition in a friendly, family-like atmosphere. Because capacity on the islands is limited, the number of participants is capped, ensuring an exclusive running experience.
course_highlights: A stage race across seven East Frisian Islands, with approximately 10 km per stage
Routes along beaches, dune landscapes and the Wadden Sea UNESCO World Heritage Site
Start and finish in central locations on each island, such as the promenade on Borkum and the Kurplatz on Norderney
additional: Race-bib collection takes place on each island from approximately 1 hour after the special ferry arrives until 30 minutes before the start. Participants receive a race bib with an integrated timing chip. Changing rooms, showers and toilets are available on the islands. Bag storage is provided. The awards ceremony takes place on each island in the afternoon. Race-pack collection is also optionally available in Bensersiel on the Friday before the event. Technical shirts, technical buffs and bottles are available as merchandise. A stage race across seven North Sea islands; there is no waiting list, and the number of participants is limited because of infrastructure and ferry capacity.

name: Dahlenburger Moorlauf
description: The Dahlenburg Moor Run is a popular community race with manual timekeeping, attracting around 200 participants each year. The event offers races for children, walking, and two main races over 4,600 m and 8,800 m. The course is flat and mostly paved, and the children’s races take place on the tartan track. The event is known for its friendly atmosphere and picturesque setting in the Dahlenburg Moor.
course_highlights: Flat, mostly paved course
Children’s races on the tartan track
Run through the picturesque setting of the Dahlenburg Moor
additional: Race number pickup from 08:30 at the DSK sports facility/Dornweg in Dahlenburg. Late entries are possible up to 30 minutes before the respective start for an additional fee of €3.00. Manual timekeeping. Showers are available at the swimming pool (admission required) or in the clubhouse. Refreshments include drink stations along the course, as well as coffee, cake, and soft drinks at the sports field. Parking is available in front of the swimming pool and the school. Courses, registration, community spirit, various types of running

name: AHRTuS-Lauf mit Ahrtal-TEAM-Cup
description: The AHRTuS Run is a club-organized race day above the Calvary Hill in Ahrweiler, prepared by TuS Ahrweiler volunteers in Quarzkaul. The program starts with races for toddlers, children and teenagers, followed by 5 km and 10 km races and a 6.2 km Nordic walking course. The adult course runs mainly along shaded forest roads and narrow trails, with some elevation gain, including a climb through the Maibach gorge with numerous wooden bridges. The 10 km race is also the final event in the Ahrtal TEAM Cup, where club teams compete for the last points. The event combines a family-friendly atmosphere with sporting competition and offers children medals, a bouncy castle, a play bus and live music at the start and finish.
course_highlights: Shaded forest roads and narrow trails
Climb through the Maibach gorge with numerous wooden bridges
10 km race as the final event in the Ahrtal TEAM Cup
additional: The event features races for toddlers, children and teenagers, a 6.2 km Nordic walking option, finisher medals for children, a bouncy castle, a play bus and live music in the start and finish area. Around 250 runners take part. In addition to the races, the event offers family activities, finisher medals, a bouncy castle, a play bus and live music in the start and finish area.

name: Eschelbronner Schreinerdorflauf
description: The Eschelbronn Carpenter Village Run takes place on June 28, 2026, and offers an approximately 10 km course on paved paths through the Eschelbronn forest and countryside. The course is challenging but suitable for all runners. The start and finish are at the TV Heim, Schlossstraße 23, in Eschelbronn. There is also a walking course with timing after 7.5 km, which can also count towards the sports badge assessment.
course_highlights: Approximately 10 km course on paved paths
Course through the Eschelbronn forest and countryside
Challenging course profile, but suitable for everyone
additional: A walking course with timing after 7.5 km is available for the sports badge assessment. Start and finish at the TV Heim (Schlossstraße 23). The course is on paved paths. Start at 9:00 a.m.; registration from 8:00 a.m. Includes a walking category with timing after 7.5 km.

name: Schwalbacher Volkslauf - Sport gegen Armut
location: Schwalbach am Taunus, Hochtaunuskreis, Hessen, Germany
description: The Schwalbach Volkslauf is an inclusive charity run held annually by Turngemeinde 1887 e.V. Schwalbach. It offers various race distances for all age and ability groups, including 10 km, 6 km, a 3 km fun run, a 1 km handicap run and a children’s run. The event celebrates inclusion, bringing together people of different backgrounds and abilities in a welcoming atmosphere. It supports social projects and raises awareness of poverty.
course_highlights: A range of distances from 370 m to 10 km
Inclusive participation for people with and without disabilities
A welcoming atmosphere, supported by the commitment of helpers and volunteers
additional: The event features several distances, including a handicap run and a children’s run, to promote inclusion. It is supported by Lebenshilfe Main-Taunus e.V., which advocates for people with disabilities in the Main-Taunus district. The event includes multiple race distances, including races for children and people with disabilities, is sponsored by GLOBUS Eschborn, and takes place in June in Schwalbach am Taunus.

name: Tippkötter Sommerlauf in Rheine
location: Bentlager Wald, Rheine, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The 11th Tippkötter Summer Run in Rheine takes place on June 28, 2026, in Bentlage Forest and offers scenic, nature-filled routes with views of the salt works and Bentlage Monastery. The spectacular finish is in the FC Eintracht Rheine stadium, where all runners cross the finish line at the penalty spot. Music, professional commentary and surprises make this a special running experience for participants of all ages. Alongside the main race, there is also an elementary school run, making the event a family-friendly sports festival.
course_highlights: Scenic routes through Bentlage Forest
Route passing the salt works and Bentlage Monastery
Finish in the FC Eintracht Rheine stadium at the penalty spot
additional: Electronic timing with a transponder race bib. Race packets can be collected in the VIP room at FC Eintracht Rheine. Headphones are prohibited and may result in disqualification. Bambini run participants receive a participation medal. Trophies for the overall winners of the 2 km, 5 km, 5 km walking and 10 km races. Age-group awards with medals only for the 2 km race. Certificates can be printed via Race Result. Ample changing rooms and showers are available. Food and drink available on site, including drinks, fries, bratwurst, steaks and waffles. Parking is available at Rheine Zoo. The 5 km and 10 km routes are officially measured and eligible for rankings. The event takes place in June 2026 and features various race distances, electronic timing, on-site refreshments and parking at Rheine Zoo; there is no parking directly at the event venue.

description: The 19th Muko Charity Run Hannover is an inclusive event taking place on 28 June 2026 at the VfL Eintracht Hannover sports ground. It is open to all ages and ability levels, whether you run, walk or stroll, with or without a disability. The aim is to raise donations for Haus Schutzengel, a guest house for parents and patients from cystic fibrosis families, near Hannover Medical School. Sponsors donate one euro for every lap completed on the 400-metre cinder track. The run promotes community and solidarity in the fight against cystic fibrosis.
course_highlights: Lap on a 400-metre cinder track
Inclusive run for all age groups and ability levels
Event held at the VfL Eintracht Hannover sports ground
additional: The run takes place from 11:00 to 15:00. Each participant can run, walk or stroll as many laps as they like. Sponsors donate one euro per lap or a fixed total amount. A donation receipt is issued for donations of 20 euros or more. Certificates are awarded after the run. An online donation tool will be made available later. Hygiene rules must be observed; disinfectant will be available on site. Run on a 400m cinder track, donations from sponsors, online donation tool, changing rooms and showers available, no dogs allowed, refreshments at the club restaurant, children's activities, under the patronage of Tina Deeken.

description: The hella hamburg half marathon is a major running event in Hamburg, held annually on the last Sunday in June. On an officially measured, flat, paved 21.1 km course, up to 24,000 runners enjoy a unique running party through the Hanseatic city. The route passes around 50 landmarks and is accompanied by numerous event spots with DJ support and live music. The event is known for its great atmosphere and traffic-free course, secured by the police and course marshals.

Flat, fully paved point-to-point course
Around 50 landmarks and numerous event spots with live music and DJ support
additional: Sunday start from 08:30, course closes at 13:40 (maximum finish time 3:30 h). Runners born in 2010 or earlier are eligible to participate. description: The 24-Hour Burginsel Run in Delmenhorst is a challenging ultramarathon on a flat, approx. 1.3 km loop along Burginsel and the Graftwiesen. The event offers individual and team competitions, as well as a 6-hour run and a 3-hour student run. The course is closed to traffic, illuminated and mostly shaded, making it ideal for endurance runners who want to test their limits. There is a refreshment station open around the clock and a tent area for rest breaks. The German 24-Hour Running Championships are held as part of this event.
course_highlights: Flat, approx. 1.3 km loop along Burginsel and the Graftwiesen
Course closed to traffic, illuminated and mostly shaded
Automatic digital timing with live interim results
additional: The race starts on 27.06.2026 at 12:00 and ends on 28.06.2026 at 12:00. The course is certified by the DLV. A refreshment station is open around the clock and offers fruit, cereals, hot and cold drinks, as well as a hot dinner and breakfast for 24-hour runners. Showers and changing rooms are about 250 m away at the Stadtbad sports hall. Public parking and motorhome pitches are available on the Graftwiesen. Team entries include 5 starting places; each additional person costs 20 EUR. Relay participants must be registered via the link in the confirmation email. There will be a large laser show and live music in the evening. The event also includes a 3-hour student run for ages 8 and up, refreshments included, race bibs with chips, a medal for 24-hour runners, a participant limit due to high demand, and a tent area for rest.

description: The BikeNavy! Run is a unique running event that takes place on the grounds of Nordholz Sports Airfield, which is otherwise not open to the public. The course runs within the restricted zone of the Nordholz Naval Air Base and offers participants a special atmosphere, with views of historic and modern aviation. After the race, visitors can explore the AERONAUTICUM Naval Aviation and Airship Museum. The event is ideal for runners looking for an unusual and unforgettable running experience.
course_highlights: Course across the grounds of Nordholz Sports Airfield
Route within the restricted zone of the Nordholz Naval Air Base
Close to the AERONAUTICUM Naval Aviation and Airship Museum
additional: On event day, food and drinks are available from 9:00 a.m. There is a charity raffle, and entry to the “Last Man Standing” show race is free from 10:30 a.m. Various races are offered for children and adults. Ample parking is available at Nordholz Sports Airfield. The venue can also be reached by public transport and bicycle. The event features various categories, including children’s races, duathlons and cycling races, as well as entertainment, registration and charity activities. After the race, visitors can explore the nearby AERONAUTICUM Naval Aviation and Airship Museum.

name: Halderner Volkslauf
description: The Haldern Volkslauf is a long-standing race that brings young and old together and fosters a sense of community among friends and families. The event will take place again on June 28, 2026, with the half marathon remaining permanently on the program following positive feedback. The event offers a friendly atmosphere for runners of all abilities and welcomes participants.
course_highlights: Running together, young and old
Half marathon as a permanent part of the program
Event in Rees-Haldern with a family-friendly character
additional: The event includes a half marathon, online registration is open until June 22, and results from previous years are published.

name: Hardtwaldlauf 2026
description: The Hardtwaldlauf in Karlsruhe is a traditional running event, taking place for the 40th time on June 28, 2026. Races are offered over 5 km and 10 km, both running through the Hardtwald and suitable for recreational runners and competitive athletes alike. The event offers professional timing with disposable transponders and a friendly atmosphere, with certificates and prizes for various age groups. Race bibs can be collected at the venue on the day of the event from 7:30 a.m. Changing and shower facilities are available on site.
course_highlights: Runs through the Hardtwald in Karlsruhe
5 km and 10 km courses with net timing via disposable transponder
Race bibs can be collected in the tennis hall on the MTV grounds from 7:30 a.m.
additional: Late entries are possible online until half an hour before the respective start, with a late-entry fee of €2.00 per race. Parking is available along Adenauerring and at Klosterweg, but not in the large Birken car park opposite BBBank Wildpark. Changing and shower facilities are available at MTV Karlsruhe. Certificates can be printed online. Special prizes are awarded to the first three women and men in the 10 km race, as well as merchandise prizes and certificates for the age groups and the five fastest women and men in the 5 km race. The race starts and finishes on the MTV grounds, with parking available nearby. Participant information and results are available online, and the event is part of the Karlsruhe running calendar.

name: Internationaler Trierer Stadtlauf
description: The 40th International Trier City Run takes place on 28 June 2026 in Trier city centre. The new course passes through the historic setting of Germany’s oldest city, by landmarks such as the Porta Nigra and the Imperial Baths. There are suitable distances for all ability levels, from the Bambini Run for children to the half marathon as the premier event. The city run combines a sporting challenge with a sense of community and the special atmosphere of one of Germany’s most beautiful cities.
course_highlights: New course through Trier city centre
Passes historic landmarks such as the Porta Nigra and the Imperial Baths
Run through the heart of Germany’s oldest city
additional: Distances: half marathon, 10 km run, 5.4 km youth run, Bambini Run. Registration is via the external website silvesterlauf.de. The event combines sport, community and history. The organiser is CITY SPORT Trier, with a retail shop in Trier city centre. Various distances, flat courses, historic landmarks, morning start times, online registration, a participant limit of 1,800, and participation open to all age groups.

name: Kilometer für Kinder
description: Kilometer für Kids is an annual charity event launched in 2014 to support children and young people in need through sporting challenges. Participants clock up kilometres by running, cycling or swimming, then make a donation for each kilometre. The project promotes not only sport, but also social cohesion and the joy of being active. Its aim is to give children new hope after difficult experiences and to highlight the importance of physical activity in society.
course_highlights: A self-organised triathlon that participants can customise, with swimming, cycling and running
Supported group bike rides and running groups
Swimming leg at the Wiedenbrück outdoor pool
additional: Participants can put together their triathlon individually and take part as a team or relay. The kilometres clocked up are donated to a good cause. The event takes place in North Rhine-Westphalia, with the aim of holding an event in every German state in the future. Since 2014, the event has supported children's aid projects in Germany, raising almost €25,000 to date. It promotes physical activity for a good cause and takes place annually in Pronsfeld.

name: Kreuzwertheimer Landschaftsläufe
description: The Kreuzwertheim Landscape Runs offer three varied races for different age groups on 28 June 2026. The 14 km “Run into Himmelreich” course passes through a protected landscape area and vineyards, with challenging climbs. The new 7 km run around Kaffelstein features gentle climbs and beautiful views of the Main Valley. Children and teenagers can take part in a hilly 2.2 km forest run. The event is family-friendly, with team classifications, non-cash prizes and a floral surprise at the finish.
course_highlights: 14 km loop through a protected landscape area and vineyards, with approx. 300 metres of elevation gain
7 km run with gentle climbs and views of the Main Valley
Hilly 2.2 km forest run for children and teenagers
additional: Late entries are available online only from 28.6.2025 until one hour before the respective race, with a €4 late-entry fee (except for the school race). Start and finish are at the Kreuzwertheim sports ground, Philipp-Günzelmann-Weg. There is a team classification for the 14 km run (teams of two). A special prize will be awarded to the club, company or group with the most participants. Food and drinks will be available on site. All participants receive certificates; children receive a “Gold” or “Silver Running Shoe” award. Results and certificates are available online. The event includes various race distances, including children’s races, with attractive routes through vineyards and nature reserves. There are team and age-group classifications, refreshments on site, and awards in the form of trophies and medals.

name: Losheimer Trailfest
location: Losheim am See, Saar-Hunsrück, Saarland, Germany
description: The Losheim Trailfest on 27 and 28 June 2026 offers a varied trail-running experience in the Saar-Hunsrück-Hochwald premium hiking region. Participants can look forward to spectacular trails featuring bizarre rock formations, winding streams, raised bogs and romantic stream valleys. The ultra distances have been extended: the T 60 has become the 100-kilometre T 100, and the T 45 has become the 50-kilometre T 50; both routes lead around the Saarschleife. There is an age-appropriate Youth Trail for young people, and the T Ch Challenge lets runners experience different routes over two days. The event site at Losheim Seegarten is a place to relax and celebrate.
course_highlights: Spectacular trails around the Saarschleife
Bizarre rock formations, raised bogs and romantic stream valleys
Flowing trails with tough climbs and adventurous descents
additional: Shuttle bus service on Saturday from 08:30 from Losheim to the start line in Mettlach for the T 50 and T Ch. Mandatory equipment for the T 100 includes a headlamp with spare batteries, a personal cup, a mobile phone with the emergency number, rainwear and an emergency blanket. Refreshments at several stations include water, isotonic drinks, fruit, snacks and regional specialities. Massage available in the afternoon for long-distance runners. Pasta party on Friday evening (€10), bookable when registering. Dogs are allowed at the event site in Seegarten, but not in the lido. KidsRun: a short loop on the event grounds. Trail running, hiking, children’s races, scenic trails, registration deadline, participant limits

name: Ohndorfer Volkslauf
description: The Ohndorf Fun Run is a family-friendly running event held annually in Ohndorf and is part of the Schaumburg Running Series. The event offers a welcoming atmosphere for runners of all ages and ability levels. Online registration is available until the day of the event, with on-site late registration open until 30 minutes before the start. The run is attracting growing numbers of participants and offers a great opportunity to exercise together and experience a sense of community.
course_highlights: Various running distances for all ages and ability levels
Family- and team-oriented event with competitions
Traditional, family-friendly running event in Ohndorf
additional: Online registration is open until 3 p.m. on the day of the event. Late registration is available on the day of the event until 30 minutes before the start time. The Kurparklauf is canceled in 2026, so there will be no Samtgemeinde Cup scoring. Multiple running distances, team competition, family-friendly atmosphere; June weather is usually sunny.

name: Rems-Murr 24h Charity-Lauf
description: The 7th Rems-Murr 24-Hour Charity Run takes place on June 27 and 28, 2026, at Herbert-Winter-Stadion in Winnenden. The event welcomes runners, families, clubs and teams to run laps for 24 hours—whether running, walking or strolling. The run supports Clowns mit Herz Rems-Murr e.V. and the Salbengehren camp at Ebnisee, with the donations raised going to these organizations. Taking part matters more than performance, and anyone can join with a sponsor or as part of a team.
course_highlights: 24-hour run at Herbert-Winter-Stadion in Winnenden
Set in beautiful surroundings with plenty of woodland and Ebnisee
Refreshments include water, fruit and cereal bars; other food and drinks are available to buy
additional: You can take part individually or as a team. Each participant finds a sponsor who donates per lap or makes a one-time donation. Donation receipts are issued. Tents may be set up in designated areas, and motorhomes are allowed in the parking lot. Refreshments are available on site; participants may also bring their own supplies. 24-hour charity run, online and on-site registration, refreshments available on site, supporting local charitable projects

name: run + fun in Tuttlingen
description: run&fun Tuttlingen is a versatile running event taking place on June 27 and 28, 2026, in Tuttlingen. The event offers a wide range of competitions, including the B. Braun Marathon, half marathon, relay races, Nordic walking, and children’s and youth races. The courses are mostly flat, running along the Danube and through the town, making for a fast and enjoyable running experience. The event is organized by several Tuttlingen clubs and the town, creating a friendly, family-oriented sporting atmosphere.
course_highlights: Flat course with only 28 meters of elevation gain
Route along the Danube and through Tuttlingen
Start and finish at the Tuttlingen festival grounds
additional: Online registration opens on 15.11.2025 and closes on June 9, 2026, at 24:00. Late registration is possible until one hour before the start, but a race place is not guaranteed. The marathon and half-marathon courses are flat and run over two laps (marathon) or one lap (half marathon), with the start and finish at the Tuttlingen festival grounds. All participants receive medals; non-cash prizes are awarded to places 1–3 in each age group. Bag drop is available at the start. Runners may use their own refreshments only on marathon Sunday, within a limited time window. Baby joggers are not permitted in the marathon. Accompaniment by bicycle or with assistive devices results in disqualification. A multi-day running event with various distances for all age groups; registration is via the website. It is one of Tuttlingen’s summer highlights.

name: Seester Sternenlauf

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Handicaplauf für Menschen mit Behinderungen (auch Rollstuhlfahrer/innen): 8 EUR (Begleitperson frei)

description: The Seester Star Run will take place for the tenth time on 28 June 2026. It is a charity run in support of the Kinder-Hospiz Sternenbrücke in Hamburg. The event offers various distances for runners, walkers, Nordic walkers and Bambinis, including a special 10 km loop through the historic Lindenallee at Gut Seestermühe. Grill sausages, coffee and cake will be available, and the route will be lined with decorated streets and a great atmosphere. The organising team looks forward to welcoming many participants and spectators to this joyful and successful event.
course_highlights: 10 km route through the historic Lindenallee at Gut Seestermühe
Distances of 1 km (Bambini), 3 km, 5 km and 10 km
Start and finish at Seester Primary School
additional: Start and finish at Seester Primary School, Dorfstr. 43, 25370 Seester. Parking is available exclusively on Schulsteig, a dead-end street. Late registrations are not possible; changing the race distance is free of charge up to one day before the start. Participation is at your own risk. Star Run performance shirts, tank tops and sports/gym bags can be ordered for an additional fee. The run is a charity event focused on community and giving, with various distances for runners and walkers, as well as a children's race. Participation is open to everyone and supports the important work of the children's hospice.

name: Steps for Life
description: Steps for Life is a charity run organized by SV Würtingen for the 20th time in support of a relief project. In the anniversary year of 2026, participants will raise funds for the construction of a children’s home in the remote mountain region around Musikot, Nepal. The event offers 4, 8 and 15-kilometer routes through the beautiful surroundings of the Swabian Alb. Times are recorded using a professional timing system. There is also a Kids Race and a Bambini Run on Race Day. Participants can choose between the virtual running period from June 19 to 27 and Race Day on June 28.
course_highlights: 4, 8 and 15-kilometer routes on the Swabian Alb
Professional timing system with tracking boxes at the start, intermediate points and finish
Kids Race of approx. 2 km and Bambini Run of approx. 800 m on Race Day
additional: The virtual running period is from June 19 to 27, 2026, daily from 5:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., with multiple starts allowed. On Race Day, June 28, 2026, late registrations are accepted from 8:00 to 9:00 a.m.; no registrations are accepted after that. Musical accompaniment on Race Day. Award ceremonies for age-group winners, individual participants with the most kilometers, and the team with the most kilometers. Distances of 4 km, 8 km and 15 km; sponsorship per kilometer; support for a relief project in Nepal; scenic route on the Swabian Alb.

name: Trainingslauf Bottwartal-Marathon
location: Riedstadion, Steinheim an der Murr, Baden-Württemberg, Germany
description: The Bottwartal Marathon is a running event in one of the most beautiful landscapes in southern Germany, taking runners past gentle vineyard slopes, idyllic old towns and enthusiastic crowds along the course. The route is a loop through the southern and northern Bottwartal, with varied sections through Steinheim, Murr, Gronau, Beilstein, Oberstenfeld and Großbottwar. The flat finish at the Steppi roundabout in Steinheim invites runners to make a strong final push. The marathon is for adult runners aged 18 and over and is part of a varied running programme in the Bottwartal.
course_highlights: Loop through the southern and northern Bottwartal
Pass through historic old towns such as Steinheim, Beilstein and Großbottwar
Flat finish at the Steppi roundabout in Steinheim
additional: Free monthly training runs in different pace groups on the last Sunday of the month in Steinheim. Weekly Sommerloch runs during the summer holidays, every Tuesday evening at 19:00. Year-End Run at the end of the year, featuring a 10 km run followed by punch and mulled wine. Registration for all runs is through the partner Datasport. Late entries and transfers are possible until shortly before the run. The event takes place at the Riedstadion in Steinheim an der Murr and is a popular opportunity for runners to prepare for the marathon. It is recommended that you check the details with the organiser before registering.

name: Uni-Lauf Bamberg
description: The Uni-Lauf Bamberg is an open public race and will take place for the 12th time in 2026. It offers several distances, including a 10 km main race, which also serves as the Bavarian University Championships and the Upper Franconian Championships, a 10 km relay, a 2 km girls’ race and a 500 m Bambini run. The flat, officially measured course runs through ERBA Park, along the Main-Danube Canal, through the Hain and Bamberg city centre, with picturesque views of historic buildings. The event has a family-friendly atmosphere and welcomes runners of all ages and ability levels.
course_highlights: Flat loop course with start and finish in the courtyard of the university building
The route runs along the Main-Danube Canal, through the Hain and the city centre, with views of the Old Town Hall and Michaelsberg Monastery
Relay handover at Buger Spitze at km 5.5
additional: Start times: 500 m Bambini run at 9:15 a.m., 2 km students’ race at 9:30 a.m., 10 km main race at 10:00 a.m. Late registration is available on site on race day from 8:00 to 9:30 a.m. (cash only). Water, energy drink, fruit and pastries are available in the finish area. Two refreshment stations on the 10 km course (around km 5 and km 7). Starting groups are arranged by target finish time (under 40 min, 40–50 min, 50–60 min, over 60 min). Team classification and special awards for the fastest Bamberg students and the Bavarian University Championships. Runners of all ability levels can take part; registration online only; parking available at the underground car park on the grounds; public transport by bus no. 906, Spinnerei stop.

name: Weiner Family Run 2026
description: The Weiner Family Run 2026 is a family-friendly running event organized by the FC Schwarz-Weiß Weiner running group on June 28, 2026. It is open to runners, walkers, children, and toddlers, with various distances ranging from approximately 500 meters to 10 kilometers. The focus is on enjoying physical activity and sharing the experience in a relaxed atmosphere. The start and finish area is at Sparkassenpark Weiner, and the routes run through the Weiner countryside. Participants can also enjoy a family-friendly program with an emcee and refreshments.
course_highlights: Start and finish area at Sparkassenpark Weiner
Routes through the Weiner countryside
Distances from the toddler run (approx. 500 m) to 10 km
additional: Online registration opens on February 7, 2026, via my race|result. A family-friendly program with an emcee and refreshments is available for participants. Races for all age groups include toddlers, children and teenagers, 5 km, and 10 km. Multiple race distances, family-friendly event, online registration opens February 7, 2026, start and finish at the SW Weiner Sparkassenpark.

name: Zwiefalter Berglauf
description: The 20th Zwiefalten Mountain Run takes place on 28 June 2026 in Zwiefalten and offers a varied program for runners of all abilities. The event includes several races, including the 9.8 km main mountain run, the 6 km Sparkassen Run, a 6 km fun run (Nordic walking), and children’s races. The course passes through idyllic countryside, including some protected areas, and offers a great opportunity to exercise together and have fun. The event is aimed at all ages and promotes community activity.
course_highlights: The 9.8 km main mountain run features a challenging course
The 6 km Sparkassen Run and fun run (Nordic walking)
Idyllic countryside, with sections through protected areas
additional: Race bib collection from 8:00 a.m. in the start/finish area; collection closes 20 minutes before each start. Awards ceremony from approximately 12:45 p.m. at the event venue. Showers available at the sports clubhouse. The fun run uses chip timing but has no placings; finishers are listed alphabetically. Race bib raffle with prizes for all participants. A distance-collection challenge will recognize the participants who collect the most kilometres during the awards ceremony. The event promotes physical activity for all ages and ability levels. Races: 9.8 km mountain run, 6 km run, children’s races and Nordic walking; online registration; start at the Zwiefalten sports grounds; awards ceremony from approximately 12:45 p.m.

name: Montagslauf Rund um Mackenzell
description: The Montagslauf Rund um Mackenzell is a traditional fun run held in the idyllic surroundings of Hünfeld-Mackenzell. The event offers several distances, including a children’s race, 5.3 km, 10 km, and a 14.3 km route with an additional loop. The courses pass through varied landscapes, with refreshment stations along the way. The event has a family-friendly atmosphere, with medical support provided by the Red Cross. Showers are available after the race, and untimed Nordic walking is also offered.
course_highlights: 5.3 km course through varied landscapes
10 km course with an additional 4.3 km loop for a total distance of 14.3 km
Refreshment stations and medical support provided by the Red Cross
additional: Children’s race: 2 km, start at 18:30; 5.3 km: start at 19:00; 10 km and 14.3 km: start at approx. 19:10. Untimed Nordic walking available over 5 km or 10 km. Register on site or using a form; payment in cash on site. Showers available after the race. Children’s race registration is mainly handled through schools. Courses, on-site or form-based registration, refreshments, showers, award ceremonies, and a Weißbier evening with brass-band music held in parallel.

name: Sonnwendlauf Großostheim
description: The Sonnwendlauf Großostheim is a traditional running event that attracts many running enthusiasts from the region every year. The event offers various distances for different ability levels, from children’s races to a 10 km race for ambitious runners. The course runs through scenic surroundings around Großostheim, combining a sporting challenge with a nature experience and a family-friendly atmosphere. The race is a fixture on the regional sporting calendar and welcomes recreational and competitive runners alike.
course_highlights: Courses through fields and gentle climbs
Great views around Großostheim
A range of distances from 750 m to 10 km
additional: Start times: 10 km and 6 km fun run at 09:00, beginner and youth race (1.2 km) at 10:30, children’s races (750 m) between 10:45 and 12:00. Event venue: Großostheim Sports Hall. Supported by the regional brewery Schlappeseppel. Distances: 10 km main race, 6 km fun run, 1.2 km beginner and youth race, 750 m children’s races; start times between 09:30 and 12:15; venue: Großostheim Sports Hall; on-site registration available; refreshments and awards ceremony; dogs, jogging strollers and headphones are not allowed; access only via Ringheimer Mühlstraße

name: 36. Göttinger Altstadtlauf
description: The Göttingen Old Town Run is a long-standing running event in downtown Göttingen, taking place for the 36th time in 2026. The event combines running with the special atmosphere of the old town and attracts runners of all ages. In addition to the main race, there are several school races and a popular company race with team scoring. The course runs through the historic city center and offers a lively atmosphere full of excitement and activity.
course_highlights: Course through historic Göttingen city center
Several shortened old-town loops for schoolchildren and young people
Team scoring in the company cup, with a coveted challenge trophy
additional: Race bibs can be collected on several days before the race at FIZ - Fitness and Health Center of the University of Göttingen. Company cup with special and team scoring. Cut-off times for the main race are 18:50 and 19:35. No race-day entries are possible. Contact via form and telephone hotline before the event. Online registration until June 14, 2026; no race-day entries; includes the school race and company race. Race through the city center with historic charm.

name: AOK Firmenlauf Stuttgart
description: The 19th AOK Stuttgart Company Run takes place on July 1, 2026, at 6:30 p.m. at GAZI Stadium in Stuttgart-Degerloch. The run is a popular company event that combines team spirit and exercise and takes runners through the city. In addition to the run, the event offers a varied supporting program featuring a DJ, a warm-up session, and award ceremonies. Catering is provided by Rauschenberger, and all participants receive a free VVS ticket for their journey to the event.
course_highlights: Start and finish at GAZI Stadium in Stuttgart-Degerloch
Route through the heart of Stuttgart
Group warm-up session and DJ before the start
additional: DJ program on stage from 5:00 p.m.; group warm-up shortly before the start; award ceremonies and music after finishing; free refreshments at the finish; catering by Rauschenberger; free VVS ticket for all registered runners; limited parking at the venue; travel by public transport is recommended; participant details can be changed free of charge until May 26, 2026. Routes through Stuttgart, team events, inclusion, finish-line refreshments, training plans

name: 32. Lippesee Marathon
description: The 32nd Lippesee Marathon in Paderborn-Sande is a private marathon held according to the rules of 100 Marathon Club Germany. The course consists of seven large laps of 6.1 km each, covering a total of 42.7 km around Lake Lippesee, a popular recreational area and water sports centre. Participants must provide their own refreshments, as there are no aid stations, and record their time manually. A photo of the clock must be submitted by email as proof. The race is open to runners aged 18 and over, is limited to 18 participants, and will take place only if at least five participants register.
course_highlights: 7 large laps of 6.1 km each, 42.7 km in total
Course around Lake Lippesee, a popular recreational and water sports area
Depending on the weather, the course is marked with arrows or barrier tape
additional: Time is recorded manually using a stopwatch; proof must be emailed on race day as a photo of the clock. Showers and changing rooms are not available. Participants must provide their own refreshments, as none are provided, but they pass their cars after every lap. Minimum age: 18. Participant limit: 18. Register by email no later than 6 p.m. on the day before the race, providing personal details. A liability waiver and consent to the use of photos and videos are part of the registration. Course: 7 laps of 6.1 km around Lake Lippesee; no showers or changing rooms on site; participation at your own risk; limited field (18); registration by email.

name: Büsumer Volkslauf
description: The Büsum Volkslauf is an annual running event suitable for beginners and experienced runners alike. Various distances are offered, from 400 metres for children to 10 kilometres for experienced runners. The new route follows the waterfront promenade, loops around the Familienlagune and returns, with the start and finish at Büsumer Hauptrand. The event promises a sporty day on the North Sea coast with a beautiful running backdrop.
course_highlights: New route along the waterfront promenade
Loop around the Familienlagune
Start and finish at Büsumer Hauptrand
additional: Three race distances: 400 m Bambini Run at 18:15, 5.5 km health run at 19:00, and 10 km race at 19:00. Registration is also possible by phone at 0176 96204634. Running event on the North Sea coast in Büsum, with routes for Bambini runners, health runners and competitive runners; finish at the swimming pool; registration online and by phone; start and finish at Büsumer Hauptrand; route along the promenade and around the Familienlagune.

name: Drevenacker Volksbank Abendlauf
description: The Drevenacker Volksbank Evening Run is a traditional running event in Hünxe-Drevenack, organized by the TUS Drevenack TL-Abteilung e.V. Various races take place on the event day, a Friday in July, including an officially measured 10 km road race, a 5 km jogging race with a youth category, a 5 km non-competitive walk, and children’s and toddlers’ races. The course runs through the scenic surrounding area, with the start and finish at the sports field on Buschweg. The event offers suitable competitions for all age groups and professional timing by the TAF Timing Team.
course_highlights: Officially measured 10 km course with age groups in five-year increments
5 km jogging race with a separate youth category and an officially measured course
Children’s and toddlers’ races for children and young people, with age-appropriate distances
additional: The start and finish are at the sports field on Buschweg. Women start at the tennis clubhouse, and men start in the gym on Buschweg. A €2.00 deposit is charged for the timing chip for each race number and refunded when it is returned. Late registrations are possible on the event day from 16:30 until 45 minutes before the respective start, subject to capacity. Every participant receives a certificate; prizes are awarded to the top three finishers in each age group. Online registration is available; the event is part of the Lippe-Issel-Cup; results are available online.

name: Internationaler Stadtlauf Saarburg
description: The International Saarburg City Run takes place for the 11th time on July 3, 2026, offering runners a fast course through Saarburg’s picturesque town center. The route passes through the Old Town Tunnel, along the Saar and up to Kruterberg, with the start and finish at the former bus station near the leisure and indoor swimming pool. The event attracts around 800 participants each year and concludes with an awards ceremony on the Fruchtmarkt stage as part of the Saarburg Market Days. There are different distances for runners of all ages, from the Bambini Run to the 10 km main race.
course_highlights: Fast course through Saarburg’s picturesque town center
The route passes through the Old Town Tunnel and along the Saar
The finishing straight is on Heckingstraße, with the awards ceremony on the Fruchtmarkt stage
additional: There are several races: Bambini Run (0.5 km), Youth Run (1.8 km), Company and Fun Run (5.3 km), and Main Race (10 km). The fastest runners are honored at Saarburg Gymnasium. The event traditionally takes place on Saturday evening alongside the Saarburg Market Days. In addition to the running races, the event also offers team competitions for companies and is a social highlight of the Saarburg Market Days.

name: Marburger Nachtmarathon
description: The Marburg Night Marathon will take place for the 27th time on 3 July 2026 and is the largest running event in the Central Hesse region. The event offers a classic marathon, a half marathon, and a relay marathon with up to four participants. The course passes through Marburg’s picturesque old town and along the Lahn, following a flat, record-eligible loop with views of Landgrave Castle and St. Elizabeth’s Church. The race starts in a special atmosphere at 7 p.m. in the historic market square, and the finish is at the University Stadium. All participants receive a high-quality medal featuring a notable Marburg landmark each year.
course_highlights: Flat, record-eligible loop course
Route passes through the old town and along the Lahn
Views of Landgrave Castle and St. Elizabeth’s Church
additional: The relay marathon consists of four runners, each completing a leg of around ten kilometres. The first relay runner starts in the market square, and the exchange zone is on Frankfurter Straße. Each team receives one race number attached to an elastic race-number belt. Safety pins are provided at registration. The number of participants is limited to ensure safety and an enjoyable running experience. The start and finish are at the University Stadium, about 1 km from the starting point. Course in Marburg’s city area, start at Georg-Gaßman-Stadion, relay exchange on Frankfurter Straße, registration opens on 1 March 2026

name: Rotenburger Strandfestlauf - Rotenburg rennt
location: Rotenburg an der Fulda, Hesse, Germany
price_range: 1 Euro Startgeld für Bambini, vergünstigte Preise für Schüler- und Jugendläufe
description: The Rotenburg Strandfest Run takes place every year on the first Friday in July as part of the traditional Heimat- und Strandfest in Rotenburg an der Fulda. The flat, fast course runs through the town centre and offers various events for young runners, main-race participants, elite runners and teams, as well as walking. New features include precisely measured school and elite races, plus the Beer Mile, where having fun is the main focus. The event combines sporting ambition with a friendly, social atmosphere and is a highlight of the regional running calendar.
course_highlights: Flat, fast course through Rotenburg town centre
School race: exactly 1,248 metres—a tribute to the year Rotenburg was founded
Elite race over 1.609 km (land mile), with entry requirements
additional: No on-site registration is possible; advance registration is available only through specialist portals. The 5 km and 10 km courses are no longer offered; instead, the main race covers a 1.5 km course five times. The Beer Mile has no timing and includes four alcohol-free beer breaks at 400 m intervals. Elite race entry requirements: men, 03:10 min/km; women, 03:30 min/km. Events for young runners, main-race participants, elite runners and teams, plus walking. Preparation through a running group; supported by Sparkasse.

name: Bad Essener Abendlauf
location: Kirchplatz, Bad Essen, Lower Saxony, Germany

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 3,00 EUR Schüler und Jugendliche bis 18 Jahre

description: The 29th International Bad Essen Evening Run takes place on July 3, 2026, at Kirchplatz in Bad Essen. The event offers a family-friendly atmosphere, with races for all ages and ability levels, including a Bambini run, a schoolchildren’s race, a relay, an open race, and a 10 km main race. A particular highlight is the new relay, with a shortened 6 x 400 m course that makes it easier for more children, young people, and adults to take part. Food and drinks will be available at Kirchplatz. Participants from the partner town of Bolbec, France, traditionally take part, underscoring the event’s international character.
course_highlights: Relay race with a 6 x 400 m course and just two changeover points
Three-lap 10 km main race starting and finishing at Kirchplatz in Bad Essen
Drinks available on the course in hot weather
additional: The Bambini run has no registration or entry fee. Late registration is available on the event day until 30 minutes before the race for a €2 fee. Race numbers can be collected at the venue on race day until approximately 30 minutes before the start. A drinks and sausage stand will be available at Kirchplatz. Multiple race distances, registration on-site and online, family-friendly event, international participants, food and drinks available on-site.

name: Brunnenfestlauf
description: The 17th Brunnenfest Run on 3 July 2026 in Reute offers runners a varied program on paved local roads. The main event is an officially measured 10 km course with timing and classification according to DLO age groups. There are also children’s and youth races, school relays, a fun run and Nordic walking. The event is family-friendly, with shower and changing facilities and refreshments at the village square.
course_highlights: Officially measured 10 km course on paved local roads
A varied selection of races for Bambini, children, youth and school relay teams
Timing by raceresult, with rankings suitable for best lists
additional: Race number distribution starts at 16:00 at the race office in the village square. Shower and changing facilities are available at Durlesbachhalle. Awards ceremonies will take place in stages after the races at the village square. Late entries are possible up to 30 minutes before the start for an additional fee. Registration by 1 July 2026; refreshments at the village square; course route through Reute.

name: Kadeloop
description: De Moore DRV-Kadeloop in Schipluiden is een traditionele hardloopwedstrijd die sinds 1978 jaarlijks plaatsvindt op de eerste zaterdag van juli. De hoofdafstand is 12 km door het groene Midden-Delfland en over de Vlaardingsekade terug naar Schipluiden. Daarnaast zijn er een 5 km loop en een jeugdronde van 1 en 2 km. De loop staat bekend om zijn mooie natuur en gezellige sfeer en maakt deel uit van het Zomer Runcircuit.
course_highlights: 12 km route door het groene Midden-Delfland
Loop over de Vlaardingsekade terug naar Schipluiden
Jeugdronde van 1 en 2 km speciaal voor kinderen
additional: Startnummers afhalen voor kinderen van 10:00-11:00 uur, overige afstanden 11:00-13:00 uur bij kantine VV Schipluiden. Parkeren mogelijk bij VV Schipluiden. Digitale tijdregistratie met chip bij 5 en 12 km. Waterposten onderweg en bij finish. Prijsuitreiking direct na kinderloop, 5 km rond 15:00 uur, 12 km rond 15:30 uur in kantine VV Schipluiden. Na-inschrijving is niet mogelijk, inschrijven alleen online tot 2 juli 2027 23:59 uur. Startnummer overdraagbaar tot 2 juli 21:00 uur via inschrijfsite. Afstanden: 12 km, 5 km, jeugdloop (1 en 2 km); activiteiten zoals Nordic walking en wandelen; locatie: Schipluiden, Midden-Delfland

description: The Schwandorf Charity City Run takes place for the 20th time on June 20, 2026, offering runners of all ages a varied selection of events. The event combines sporting ambition with social commitment, as net proceeds go to local nonprofit organizations such as Wasserwacht Schwandorf and Bund Naturschutz Schwandorf. Events range from the Bambini Run to school and main races, as well as Nordic walking and a Run & Bike team competition. All participants receive a charity medal and an online certificate, and medical support helps ensure their safety. The event is family-friendly and also features a Stutz’n relay rally as a fun special event.
course_highlights: A variety of distances from 200 m to 10 km, including the Bambini Run, school races, main race and Run & Bike
Courses can be viewed digitally on Google Maps, and the Zwergerl Run takes place at Sepp-Simon Stadium
Nordic walking with timing and walking without poles are also available
additional: Late registration and bib collection are possible on the day of the event during various time windows until 1:30 p.m. All participants receive a Charity City Run medal and an online certificate. Medical support is provided by the Johanniter local branch in Schwandorf. Children and school students receive small surprises. Drinks, bratwurst rolls, coffee and cake are sold for charity. Registration deadline: June 14, 2026; family-friendly; net proceeds go to Wasserwacht Schwandorf, Bund Naturschutz Schwandorf and the self-help group for people affected by post-COVID, post-vaccine syndrome and ME/CFS.

name: 10. Hochkippenlauf
description: The 10th Hochkippenlauf takes place on 4 July 2026 at Stadion Profen and is organized by SV Eintracht Profen. Various races are offered for different age groups, from a children’s race to distances for young people and 10 km races for adults. The event is part of a sports festival running from 3 to 5 July 2026. The race is a great opportunity for sports enthusiasts of all ages to compete in a family-friendly atmosphere.
course_highlights: 400 m children’s race (one lap of the stadium)
Distances of 2.1 km, 4.2 km and 5 km for young people
10 km race for U18, U20 and adults
additional: The race is part of a sports festival running from 3 to 5 July 2026. The children’s races take place over one lap of the stadium. The race is held at Stadion Profen, with warm, sunny weather in July. It offers a family-friendly atmosphere and the opportunity to win prizes in various categories.

name: 46. Küstenkanallauf
description: The 46th Küstenkanallauf takes place on 04.07.2026 in Friesoythe. The event offers races over 22 km, 11 km and 5.5 km, as well as walking and hiking routes. The scenic course runs along the Küstenkanal and is suitable for runners of all ability levels. This traditional event is organised by KC Ikenbrügge von 1971 e. V.
course_highlights: Scenic course along the Küstenkanal
Distances of 5.5 km, 11 km and 22 km
Walking and hiking routes available
additional: Start times: Runners in the 5.5 km, 11 km and 22 km races start at 17:00; walking and hiking start at 16:15. Registration is via an online form on the website or through the contact option, providing your name, year of birth, club and town. This is a local event with a friendly atmosphere that attracts numerous runners from the region each year. Registration, results and further details are available on the official website and in the race information.

name: 9. Bremer Brückenlauf
price_range: ab 8,00 € bis 45,00 € je nach Kategorie und Frühbucherstatus
description: The Bremer Brückenlauf on July 4, 2026, invites runners to experience Bremen from a unique perspective. The course crosses bridges spanning the Weser, the Kleine Weser and the Werdersee, offering a maritime atmosphere in the heart of the city. Several distances are available, including a half marathon, 10 km run, 5 km run, a special 5 km underwear run and children’s races. The event promises good spirits, a summery atmosphere and breathtaking views of Bremen and the Weser.
course_highlights: Run across several bridges in Bremen
Course over the Weser, Kleine Weser and Werdersee
Officially measured, record-eligible courses
additional: Optional medal engraving (€10 for adults, €7.50 for children). Start times vary by distance, from 16:30 (underwear run) to 18:15 (5 km and 10 km walking). All main races are measured by the DLV and are record-eligible. Children’s races are measured privately. Walkers and Nordic walkers are listed in alphabetical order in the finish results. Participation rules and age categories are clearly defined. Loop course with official measurement, age categories and competition categories; medal engraving available; Nordic walking included.

name: Benkhauser Schlosslauf
location: Schloss Benkhausen, Espelkamp, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
price_range: 600 m Kinderlauf kostenlos, 2 km Schülerlauf 4,00 € (bis 14.06.), 6,5 km 12,00 € (bis 14.06.), 10,8 km 12,00 € (bis 14.06.), 20,8 km 12,00 € (bis 14.06.), Preise steigen nach dem 14.06.
description: The Benkhausen Castle Run is a sporting event taking place for the second time in 2026, set in the unique surroundings of Benkhausen Castle. The event offers varied running routes along paved side roads and footpaths in beautiful Benkhausen. The start and finish are at Benkhausen Castle Square, where race bibs are also distributed. The event is open to running enthusiasts of all ages and includes various distances, including children’s and schoolchildren’s races.
course_highlights: Running routes along paved side roads and footpaths in beautiful Benkhausen
Start and finish at historic Benkhausen Castle Square
Kilometre markers along the route for guidance
additional: Late registration is possible on race day from 12:30 p.m. until 60 minutes before the start, provided the participant limit has not been reached; a late-registration fee of €2 applies. The number of participants is limited to 200 runners per main race (6.5 km, 10.8 km, 20.8 km), with a maximum of 600 registrations in total. Race packs will be available from 30.06.2026 at Drogerie Emmerling and on race day at the castle square. Timing uses disposable-chip technology. Showers and changing facilities are available at Benkhausen Primary School. All participants in the children’s and schoolchildren’s races receive medals; there is no timing or awards ceremony. The well-known announcer Heino Krüger will accompany the races. Registration opens on 01.02.2026; late registration is available on site; the participant limit for the main races is 200 per distance, with a maximum of 600 registrations in total; chip timing; event held as part of a sports festival

name: Eicherscheider Heckenlauf mit Halbmarathon 2026
description: The 46th Eicherscheid Hedge Run with half marathon takes place on 4 July 2026 in Simmerath-Eicherscheid in the Eifel. The races run through the hilly beech-hedge landscape around Eicherscheid, a Federal Gold Village on the edge of Eifel National Park. Events are offered over 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon (21.0975 km), each run on a hilly loop course. Children’s and youth events are also part of the event. Start times are staggered through the afternoon and evening, making for a relaxed participation.
course_highlights: Hilly loop courses through the beech-hedge landscape
Route through Eicherscheid, a Federal Gold Village on the edge of Eifel National Park
Family-friendly event with children’s and youth competitions
additional: The events have staggered start times: 5 km at 15:45, 10 km at 16:35 and the half marathon at 18:00. All events finish at the same location. RUNME Premium is required for exact finish-location details. Children’s and youth events are also offered; further information is available in the organizer’s official race announcement. The event is family-friendly, with start times varying by distance. Registration is via the official website.

name: Fichtelgebirgsmarathon mit Halbmarathon und 10km-Lauf
description: The Fichtelgebirge Marathon on July 4, 2026, is the largest running event in the Fichtelgebirge, with three different courses for all ages. The races feature challenging elevation gains and beautiful scenery, guaranteeing participants a unique experience in nature. For over 20 years, the event has been organized by sports-loving club members of IfL-Fichtelgebirge, who ensure everything runs smoothly. Online registration is open until July 2, 2026.
course_highlights: Marathon with 42 km and 800 meters of elevation gain
Half marathon with 21 km and 400 meters of elevation gain
10 km run with 225 meters of elevation gain and a finish in Kurpark Bad Alexandersbad
additional: The event is organized by volunteer club members. There are three courses with different elevation profiles and distances. All courses finish in Kurpark Bad Alexandersbad. Detailed course information is available on Komoot. The event is known for its challenging course with significant elevation gain and the beautiful natural scenery of the Fichtelgebirge. Online registration is open until July 2, 2026.

name: Hochstraßenlauf
description: The Hochstraßenlauf in Weisendorf is a traditional running event taking place for the 40th time on July 4, 2026. The start and finish are at the Weisendorf Local History Association Museum. Due to the high temperatures in recent years, the start time has been moved to the morning to offer runners better conditions. The event is open to runners of all ages and offers a family-friendly atmosphere, with scoring for the Weisendorf town championship.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the Weisendorf Local History Museum
Run through the surroundings of Weisendorf on scenic routes
Various age categories and scoring for the Weisendorf town championship
additional: Please bring safety pins for your race number. The terms of participation and a data protection form must be brought for children under 16. To be included in the Weisendorf town championship, provide the postcode 91085 and register accordingly. The event takes place in the morning to avoid the heat and offers a wide range of running and walking options. Registration is open until July 2, 2026.

name: Honiglauf des TuS Horn
description: The traditional TuS Horn Honey Run offers running and walking routes for all age groups around Horn. The event is known for its family atmosphere, with the winners rewarded with a jar of the coveted Horner honey. A range of distances, from the Bambini race to the 10 km run, makes it possible for children, teenagers, and adults to take part. The event takes place at the Horn community center and combines sporting ambition with fun and a sense of community.
course_highlights: Running and walking routes around Horn
Distances from 150 m to 10 km for all age groups
Winners are rewarded with Horner honey
additional: Late entries are possible up to 1 hour before the respective start, with a late-entry fee of €2.00. The start and finish are at the Horn community center, Hauptstr. 18. Showers are available for women at the community center and for men at the clubhouse at the sports ground. The top finishers receive trophies or medals and a jar of honey; all participants receive certificates and prizes. Honey is raffled among the walkers who are present. No specific information is available about course length, registration, or other race details.

name: Stadtlauf - Nördlingen läuft rund
description: The Stadtlauf Nördlingen läuft rund takes place on 4 July 2026 and offers races for children, school students, adults and walkers. The approximately 6 km main race runs through and around Nördlingen’s historic old town. Team spirit and the enjoyment of exercise are the main focus, and every participant receives a medal at the finish. The event is open to individual and group entries and encourages people to enjoy running together.
course_highlights: Approximately 6 km main race through and around Nördlingen’s old town
Children’s and school races with 400 m and 800 m laps
Start and finish area at the Market Square, with the route passing Daniel, Obstmarkt, Hallgasse and Schäfflesmarkt
additional: Advance registration is possible until 19 June 2026. Late entries are possible on the event day for an additional fee of 2 euros. If participant numbers are high, school races will start separately for girls and boys. There are individual and team rankings, and the three fastest teams in the main race (6 km) will be recognised. There is no awards ceremony for walkers; the focus here is on health. Tables for socialising after the race can be reserved by email. Distances: 400 m children’s race, 7 km main race; medals for all finishers; prizes for the fastest company teams and those with the most participants; registration until 19 June 2026; the event takes place in all weather.

name: 01. Okertalsperren Ultra-Marathon
location: Altenau im Harz, Goslar, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The 1st Okertalsperren Ultra Marathon takes place on July 4, 2026, in Altenau in the Harz Mountains. The course covers 47.4 km and consists of three laps of a 15.8 km, mostly flat route around the main arm of the Okertalsperre reservoir. The route follows the forebay, crosses the dam and the main dam, and offers a scenic run with only gentle climbs. The event is suitable for experienced runners. Participants are advised to bring their own refreshments, and they are responsible for timing themselves. After the race, participants receive certificates by email, and the results are published on the website.
course_highlights: Three 15.8 km laps around the Okertalsperre reservoir
Crossing the forebay dam and the main dam
Mostly flat course with gentle climbs
additional: Participants are advised to bring their own refreshments, for example from the trunk of their car. Runners time themselves using a running watch or phone and submit proof by photo or screenshot via email to the organizer. Certificates are sent as PDFs by email. Results are published on the website. The race takes place on July 4, 2026. It is a self-supported event with no explicit entry fee, and participants must provide proof of their results. The course consists of three 15.8 km laps around the reservoir.

name: 23. Schneekopflauf
location: Schmiedefeld am Rennsteig, Thüringer Wald, Germany
description: The Schneekopflauf is one of the most beautiful and challenging mountain races in Germany, held in the Thuringian Forest. The route runs from Schmiedefeld via Großer Finsterberg to Schneekopf and covers 12.7 and 22.2 kilometres, with plenty of climbs and elevation gain. This race is particularly suitable for experienced runners who want to test their limits. Since 2025, there has also been a Schneekopf hike for Nordic walkers and hikers, who are also rewarded with a medal at the summit.
course_highlights: 12.7 km and 22.2 km routes with challenging climbs
Elevation gain from the start to the summit at 978 m
Run through the Thuringian Forest with breathtaking views
additional: Late registration is possible from 26.06.2026 until 30.06.2026, 23:59. Cancellation is possible until 30.04.2026 with a 50% refund, minus a EUR 5 processing fee. Switching from 12.7 km to 22.2 km is possible by paying the difference; no refund is available for switching in the other direction. Entries are non-transferable. Steep, challenging, elevation gain, mountain race, Nordic walking, hike
